content.p: and the integral \displaystyle \int_{ {{start}} }^{ {{end}} }f(x)dx. Express this integral as the sum of limits of proper integrals. Note that there are vertical asymptotes at x={{ass1}}, {{ass2}} and {{ass3}}.

p.m: \displaystyle \lim_{c_1\to {{lim1}}^- } \left( \int_{ {{start}} }^{c_1} f(x) dx\right) + \lim_{c_2\to {{lim1}}^+ } \left( \int_{ c_2 }^{ {{cut1}} } f(x) dx\right) + \lim_{c_3\to {{lim2}}^- } \left( \int_{ {{cut1}} }^{c_3} f(x) dx\right) + \lim_{c_4\to {{lim2}}^+ } \left( \int_{ c_4 }^{ {{cut2}} } f(x) dx\right) + \lim_{c_5 \to \infty } \left( \int_{ {{cut2}} }^{ c_5 } f(x) dx\right)

\displaystyle \lim_{c_1\to -\infty } \left( \int_{c_1 }^{ {{cut1}} } f(x) dx\right) + \lim_{c_2\to {{lim1}}^- } \left( \int_{ {{cut1}} }^{ c_2 } f(x) dx\right) + \lim_{c_3\to {{lim1}}^+ } \left( \int_{ c_3 }^{ {{cut2}} } f(x) dx\right) + \lim_{c_4\to {{lim2}}^- } \left( \int_{ {{cut2}} }^{ c_4 } f(x) dx\right) + \lim_{c_5 \to {{lim2}}^+ } \left( \int_{ c_2 }^{ {{end}} } f(x) dx\right)
